runs.str: Collective dephasing of a Rydberg superatom under imperfect blockade

We study how an ensemble of atoms that shares a single Rydberg excitation, a superatom, loses
coherence when the Rydberg blockade is imperfect. Pairs of atoms with a weak interaction
admit doubly excited states, and the resulting leakage acts as a collective dephasing channel. We

The collective dephasing also explains a feature that an
incoherent loss model cannot reproduce. When the drive
is detuned, the measured contrast recovers partially at
long times, a revival that comes from the phase coher-
ence between the leaked pairs and the superatom. In our
model this revival appears naturally, because the virtual
excursions to the doubly excited states are coherent and
interfere with the direct Rabi oscillation.

We have shown that an imperfect Rydberg blockade
acts on a superatom as a collective dephasing channel
with a rate that scales with the square of the atom num-
ber. The effective master equation reproduces the mea-
sured decay of the collective Rabi oscillation and the re-
vival at finite detuning, and it provides a design rule for
the readout fidelity of superatom experiments.
